subject: Evaluation gates, commit schedule and burst safeguards for Dedicated GPU pool
messages:
From: Claire Nguyen <claire@opsly.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluation gates and commit schedule for Dedicated GPU pool

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the throughput numbers looked promising. We want to formalize an evaluation MAP so we can align procurement, engineering, and platform ops. A couple of priorities from our side:

- Clear evaluation gates with success metrics (P95 latency < 350ms, 99th percentile tail recovery during 1k rps load test).
- A staged commit schedule tied to MAP gates so we can justify a reserved GPU pool purchase to finance.
- A burst policy (temporary overcommit) for production spikes — we need a guardrail so we aren’t exposed to runaway costs.

Can you share a proposed MAP with milestone-linked pricing and an example ramp (3/6/12 months) plus the burst clause language you typically recommend? Our procurement lead (Jordan Li) wants to see it for initial redlines.

Attaching our initial evaluation checklist. If possible, can we aim to close terms by the end of next week?

Cheers,
Claire Nguyen
Head of MLOps, Opsly
claire@opsly.ai

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Evaluation gates and commit schedule for Dedicated GPU pool

Hi Claire — appreciated the thoughtful list. I put together a draft MAP that ties milestones to commits and pricing tiers (attached). High-level summary below.

Milestones (example MAP):
1) Pilot (0–6 weeks): 2x A100-equivalent slots, test harness + validation. Success gate: run 1k rps synthetic test; P95 < 350ms.
2) Scale phase 1 (month 2–3): Reserve 8-slot pool (baseline throughput for low-latency inference). Conditional commit: 25% of 12-month commitment upon successful gate.
3) Scale phase 2 (month 4–6): Expand to 20-slot pool. Additional commit triggers at defined MAP gates — negotiated staircase ramp.

Pricing & term suggestions (illustrative):
- 12-month term baseline pricing per-slot (USD) with stepped discounts at each committed tranche (example: 10% initial discount, 15% at 8+ slots, 20% at 20+ slots).
- Minimums: monthly min billing at 50% of reserved capacity during ramp months to keep unit economics predictable.

Burst clause (recommended guardrail):
- Included burst credit: up to 10% additional capacity above reserved pool for short windows (max 2 hours per day, 10 hours per month) at no extra charge.
- Excess burst beyond credits billed at a predefined overage rate (e.g., 1.6x standard per-slot rate) with daily cap to avoid runaway charges.
- Auto-fallback: when sustained >30% above reserved for >48 hours, system will trigger an escalation and provisioning recommendation to convert burst to temporary paid capacity or adjust the reserved pool.

Operational notes:
- We can instrument the MAP with tracing and token-level cost dashboards so your SREs see the cost signal during stress events.
- We'll include a canary fallback to a cheaper quantized model variant if latency targets are at risk during high load (optional).

Next steps:
- I attached a redline-friendly MAP PDF (Opsly-MAP-eval-draft.pdf). If Jordan has procurement questions we can fold them into the next revision — Ben and Aditya are looped for pricing/legal/technical details.

Happy to jump on a 30-min sync tomorrow to walk through.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is very helpful. A few clarifications from procurement/finance:

- Can we tighten the minimum billing during ramp months to 25% instead of 50% for the first two months? Opsly needs flexibility early on while we validate traffic patterns.
- We need explicit rollback language for the first gate (if latency or correctness regressions appear, we retain the right to halt further commits and revert to best-effort hosted capacity).
- Please include sample invoice language and a short example of how overage charges would be calculated in a high-traffic event.

Jordan Li (procurement) is now on the thread and will send a short list of commercial questions. We are aiming to finish internal approvals by Friday; if you can get a redlineable agreement to legal today/tomorrow, that would be ideal.

Claire

Looping back with a negotiation play that balances Opsly flexibility and Redwood unit economics — propose we offer the following in the next redline: 

Commercial proposal (to put in the redline):
- Term: 12 months with staged commit staircase at months 1/3/6.
- Initial reserved pool: 8 slots for months 0–2; commit triggers to move to 20 slots by month 6 assuming MAP gates pass.
- Billing minimum: 25% of reserved capacity for months 0–2 (per Claire request), 50% for months 3–6, then full reserved billing after month 6.
- Discounts: 12% off list at initial commit; additional 6% at 8+ slots; additional 8% at 20+ slots (stacking to a max 26%).

Burst and overage language:
- Included burst credits: 10% daily burst (up to 2 hours/day) and 10 hours/month aggregated free burst.
- Overage rate: 1.5x standard per-slot rate billed hourly beyond included credits.
- Caps & escalation: daily overage cap at 50% of monthly commitment; sustained >30% for 48h triggers ops review and automatic capacity recommendation.

Legal & procurement ops:
- Provide a redline-ready addendum that includes rollback language for failed gates, sample invoice lines, and a short example calculation for a 3x traffic spike event.
- Aditya: please prepare a short appendix explaining operational controls (KV cache behavior, canary fallback to quantized variants, and telemetry hooks we will expose).
- Hannah: propose a 60-min sync with Opsly procurement tomorrow at 10:00 AM PT to walk through items and capture redlines.

I will ask legal to prepare the initial DocuSign bundle once we get their redlines — please confirm if Opsly wants a multi-sig sign flow or single-signer procurement.

Thanks team — this keeps momentum while protecting margins.
